descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a single center, open-label, dose-escalation/expansion clinical study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of Fourth-Generation CAR-T, and determine the recommended dose of the CAR T-cells for patients with Multiple Myeloma，B-cell lymphoma and other hematologic malignancies.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a single center, open-label, dose-escalation/expansion clinical study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Fourth-Generation CAR-T in the Treatment of Multiple Myeloma，B-cell lymphoma and other hematologic malignancies.. -Prior to Fourth-Generation CAR-T cells infusion, subjects will receive lymphodepleting therapy with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide. After infusion, the investigators will observe the characteristics of dose limited toxicity (DLT), and determine the maximum tolerable agent MTD and RP2D were confirmed. To provide basis for the dosage and treatment plan of cell products in follow-up clinical trials. Meanwhile, subjects will be followed for side effects and effect of the CAR-T.

armGroups.label: Phase 1:Low dose group
armGroups.description: Infusion of CAR T-cells by single dose of 0.5×10\^6 CAR-T cells/kg

armGroups.label: Phase 1: Medium dose group
armGroups.description: Infusion of CAR T-cells by single dose of 1.5×10\^6 CAR-T cells/kg

armGroups.label: Phase 1: High dose group
armGroups.description: Infusion of CAR T-cells by single dose of 5.0×10\^6 CAR-T cells/kg

armGroups.label: Phase 2a: RP2D
armGroups.description: After all subjects in the Phase 1 dose-escalation study completed DLT observation, RP2D was determined based on the analysis results for the phase 2a expansion study.

interventions.name: CAR-T
interventions.description: CAR T-cell therapy involves autologous chimeric antigen receptor T-cells, capable of targeting human B cell maturation antigen (BCMA) ,CD19 or CD-7 etc. target molecules of other hematologic malignancies.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Number of patients with dose-limiting toxicity (DLT)
primaryOutcomes.description: For DLT evaluation, severity (grade) is classified according to common terminology criteria for adverse events version 4.03 (CTCAE v4.03).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 30 days of receiving CAR T-cells transfusion therapy

primaryOutcomes.description: At least 6 subjects in the MTD dose group must complete the DLT assessment.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 30 days of receiving CAR T-cells transfusion therapy

primaryOutcomes.description: Safety will be assessed by adverse events (AEs), which include clinically significant abnormalities identified during medical tests (e.g. laboratory tests, electrocardiogram, imaging examinations or physical examinations). AEs will be coded by Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MeDRA) and their severity will be graded according to the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE, version 4.03).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Minimum 2 years after CAR T-cells infusion (Day 1)

primaryOutcomes.description: To determine after all subjects in the Phase 1 dose-escalation study completed DLT observation
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 1 year

primaryOutcomes.description: The definition of ORR is the proportion of subjects achieving sCR, CR, VGPR, or PR confirmed by efficacy reassessment after a minimum interval of three months. ORR is calculated as (sCR+CR+VGPR+PR) divided by the total number of cases of Multiple Myeloma, or (CR+PR) divided by the total number of cases of B-cell lymphoma and other hematologic malignancies, multiplied by 100%.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.description: The definition of sCRR is the proportion of subjects achieving sCR confirmed by efficacy re-assessment after a minimum interval of three months. Efficacy assessment for multiple myeloma only.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.description: The time interval from the first administration of the investigational drug to the first observation of disease progression is calculated, considering the date of entry for patients who died for reasons other than disease progression before progression occurred.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.description: OS is the time from the start of cell infusion to the death of the subject.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 2 years
